issues.legal_issue: Instructions for conducting a survey settlement that describe an existing arrangement do not constitute an express reservation of the State’s rights to trees.
material_facts: A survey settlement had been completed in the relevant village before the land revenue law came into force.
The State relied on a provision in rules for classifiers issued to guide the survey settlement, whose explanation described the rights relating to trees on the lands.

The Court found that the classifiers’ rules were instructions for carrying out the settlement and that the provision described an assumed existing state of affairs rather than making an express reservation.
issues.conclusion: The provision in the rules for classifiers was not an express order reserving the State’s right to the trees within the meaning of section 75(1) of the Mysore Land Revenue Act, 1964.
issues.legal_principle: Section 75(1) deems the State’s right to trees in land to have been conceded to the occupant, except for trees reserved by an express order made at or about the original survey settlement or by a notification made and published at or after that settlement. Rules intended to guide classifiers in conducting a settlement, which describe an assumed state of affairs rather than make an express declaration, do not amount to such an express order. The Court relied on the context and language of Rule 10 of the Rules for Classifiers; it cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_tree_reservation and prior_survey_settlement and claimed_state_tree_reservation and instrument_is_classifier_guidance and instrument_describes_existing_arrangement

predicates.appeal_concerning_tree_reservation: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether an instrument reserved the State’s rights to trees.
predicates.prior_survey_settlement: The original survey settlement for the relevant land was completed before the applicable land revenue law came into force.
predicates.claimed_state_tree_reservation: The State relies on an instrument as reserving its rights to trees on the land.
predicates.instrument_is_classifier_guidance: The instrument forms part of instructions guiding classifiers in conducting a survey settlement.
predicates.instrument_describes_existing_arrangemen: The instrument describes an assumed existing arrangement rather than expressly declaring a reservation of rights.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a claimed tree reservation following a prior survey settlement, an instrument that is classifier guidance and describes an existing arrangement is not an express tree reservation.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the validity of a rule need not be decided when the rule is repealed during the appeal and the requested relief is confined to that rule.
material_facts: The appellants sought to have the forest rule declared invalid and sought a permit as relief.
The challenged rule was deleted while the appeal was pending.
The appellants did not seek permission to amend their petition after the deletion.
issues.conclusion: The Court treated the challenge to the rule’s validity as academic and did not decide its merits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the validity question had become academic because the challenged rule had been deleted during the appeal and the appellants had not amended their requested relief. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this point.

predicates.appeal_challenging_a_rule: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity of a rule.
predicates.challenged_rule_repealed_during_appeal: The rule challenged in the appeal was repealed while the appeal was pending.
predicates.requested_relief_limited_to_challenged_r: The requested relief remained confined to the challenged rule after its repeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a rule that is repealed during the appeal and the requested relief remains confined to that rule, the validity issue is not adjudicated.
